title: Creek Kids Club Extended Day Program Terms: One Open Enrollment per Student
content:
**Clause.** Under the Creek Kids Club Extended Day Program a household may hold enrollments for any number of its students, and each enrollment covers one student. A registration is accepted only when the student has no other Creek Kids Club enrollment for the same school year in status registered, waitlisted, active or suspended for nonpayment. A student who needs a different plan keeps the existing enrollment and moves through a plan change; a second registration is never opened for the same student and school year. Enrollments closed as withdrawn, dismissed or ended do not count, so a withdrawn student may register again for the same school year, subject to every admission rule.

**Limits.** The household has no limit on the number of enrollments. Each student may have at most 1 open enrollment per school year.

## What the records must show

The test runs on the program's own enrollment records, never on what the family states. It matches the student and the school year of the registration against the status of every other enrollment that student holds for that school year.

| Student's other enrollment for the same school year | Effect on a new registration |
|---|---|
| none | the registration may be accepted |
| registered, waitlisted, active or suspended for nonpayment | not accepted |
| withdrawn, dismissed or ended only | does not count; the registration may be accepted, subject to every admission rule |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A household registers three siblings for the same school year. Each one gets their own enrollment, and none blocks another, because the test looks at each student separately.
- A student's enrollment for the year is waitlisted, and the family now wants a different plan. A second registration is not opened. The student keeps the waitlisted enrollment, and a different plan is reached through a plan change.
- A student withdrew from care in the fall and the family wants care again in the spring of the same school year. The withdrawn enrollment does not count, so a new registration may be accepted once every admission rule is met.
- An enrollment for the previous school year is still open. It does not count against a registration for the new school year, because the test compares enrollments of the same school year.
